ops_013:n1.prompt:
You are helping me choose a Mobile Device Management (MDM) platform for our company laptop fleet as part of SOC 2 audit prep. Please research and compare three well-known MDM vendors: Jamf, Kandji, and Microsoft Intune.

First, ask me for any missing context you need: our approximate device count, the mix of operating systems (macOS/Windows/Linux), whether we already use Apple Business Manager, our monthly/annual budget range, and whether we use Microsoft 365/Azure AD already (which could favor Intune).

Then research each vendor covering: pricing model and rough cost at our fleet size, ease of enrolling devices via Apple Business Manager (if relevant), support for baseline policies we need (disk encryption enforcement, screen lock timeout, OS update enforcement), quality of compliance reporting (can it export evidence suitable for SOC 2 audits), and any notable integration or support tradeoffs.

Produce a comparison table (vendor, cost estimate, platform support, ease of setup, compliance reporting strength, notable pros/cons) and a short written recommendation stating which vendor best fits our stated constraints and why.

Do not sign up for, purchase, or commit to any vendor account. Do not enter payment details or accept any terms of service. Your job is to prepare the research, the comparison table, and a clear recommendation with rationale, then stop for human sign-off so I can make the final vendor selection myself.

Report back with: the comparison table, your top recommendation with 2-3 sentence justification, and any open questions you couldn't resolve from the context I gave you.

ops_013:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for Apple Business Manager enrollment (https://business.apple.com/), which is required before we can push MDM policies to our fleet. This step requires a verified human company representative, so you cannot submit the form or complete Apple's identity/authority verification yourself.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for any missing details needed to fill the enrollment form: our legal company name, D-U-N-S number (or note if we need to look one up), registered business address, main company phone number, our website/domain, and the name, title, and email of the person who will act as the verified enrolling representative (must have legal authority to bind the org, e.g., a founder/officer).
2. Research and summarize Apple Business Manager's current enrollment requirements and verification process (e.g., D-U-N-S lookup, phone/identity verification steps) so I know what to expect.
3. Draft all the form field values in a clean checklist/table, ready for copy-paste, based on the information I give you.
4. Note explicitly that this is an asynchronous process — after submission, Apple will independently verify the company and representative, and approval/access will arrive later. Include instructions for how I (or you, once I ask) can check enrollment status afterward.
5. Do NOT submit the form, do NOT attempt any identity/phone verification, and do NOT sign or accept Apple's terms on my behalf.

When the checklist and summary are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off so I can personally complete the verification and submission steps on business.apple.com. Report back with the prepared checklist, any open questions (e.g., missing D-U-N-S number), and a short note on what happens after I submit, so we can track it toward audit-ready MDM enrollment.

ops_013:n3.prompt:
You are helping me configure baseline device compliance policies in {{vendor}}, our MDM platform, ahead of a SOC 2 audit. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: my {{vendor}} admin console URL/tenant, the device platforms in scope (macOS, Windows, etc.), our required disk encryption method (e.g., FileVault/BitLocker), our screen lock timeout policy (e.g., lock after 5 minutes of inactivity), and our OS/app update cadence requirement (e.g., critical patches within 14 days).

Using your configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and: (1) create or edit the baseline configuration profile(s) that enforce full-disk encryption with recovery key escrow, (2) set screen lock/auto-lock policy matching my stated timeout, (3) enable automatic OS and security update enforcement per my cadence, and (4) assign these profiles to the relevant device group(s) or 'all devices' scope. Where {{vendor}} offers compliance grading or a compliance dashboard, enable it so encryption, lock, and update status are visible per device.

After configuring, verify the policies show as 'active' or 'assigned' in {{vendor}} and pull a current compliance status export or screenshot showing which devices are compliant/non-compliant against these three controls.

Done looks like: encryption, screen lock, and update policies are live in {{vendor}} and assigned to the device scope, and you have a compliance report/export ready to serve as SOC 2 evidence.

Report back with: which policies were configured, the scope/group they apply to, the compliance report location or export, and any devices currently out of compliance that need follow-up.

ops_013:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the fleet enrollment phase of our MDM rollout (device management setup, ahead of a SOC 2 audit). The physical work of unboxing, imaging, and handing laptops to distributed employees remains a human step and cannot be done by you — do not attempt to schedule shipments or physically touch hardware.

What I need from you is the preparatory groundwork so enrollment goes smoothly once devices are physically ready. Please:

1. Ask me for: the MDM platform I've chosen (e.g., Jamf, Kandji, Intune, Mosyle), whether devices are already Apple Business Manager-registered, our current employee/device roster (or where it lives, e.g., an HRIS or spreadsheet), and whether devices are new purchases (zero-touch eligible) or existing devices needing manual enrollment.
2. Draft a step-by-step enrollment runbook covering: how to trigger zero-touch/automated enrollment for ABM-registered devices, the manual enrollment process for existing/remote devices (profile installation steps an employee would follow), and how to verify a device shows as enrolled and compliant in the MDM console.
3. Draft a short, clear email/Slack message template IT can send to each employee with instructions for enrolling their own device if manual steps are required.
4. Create a tracking checklist (device/employee, enrollment method, status, date) I can use to monitor fleet enrollment progress toward 100% coverage.
5. Note any gaps — e.g., devices not in ABM, employees without accounts — that need resolution before enrollment can complete.

Report back with: the runbook, the employee message draft, the tracking checklist template, and a list of any blockers or missing inputs. Do not attempt to physically enroll, ship, or image any device — this remains a human step.

ops_013:n5.prompt:
You are helping me wire our MDM compliance reports into SOC 2 evidence via Vanta. Our fleet is already enrolled in Apple Business Manager and our MDM, with baseline policies (disk encryption, screen lock, auto-updates) pushed to all devices.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) our Vanta account/workspace details, (2) which MDM we are using, and (3) confirmation of who has admin rights to authorize integrations in both Vanta and the MDM console.

Actions to take:
1. Using your configured credentials, sign in to Vanta and locate the integrations section for device/endpoint monitoring.
2. Find and select our MDM as the integration source, then follow Vanta's connection flow to link it — this typically involves authorizing Vanta to read device compliance data from the MDM via an OAuth-style connection or API key entry in the MDM's admin console.
3. Once connected, confirm Vanta is pulling device inventory and compliance status (disk encryption, screen lock, OS/patch version) for every enrolled laptop.
4. Check Vanta's monitored devices list against our actual fleet count from the MDM to confirm full coverage — flag any missing or unenrolled devices.
5. Review Vanta's compliance dashboard for any failing checks (e.g., encryption disabled, lock screen off, outdated OS) and note them for remediation.
6. Confirm the integration is set to continuously sync so evidence stays current for the audit window.

Done looks like: Vanta shows an active, healthy connection to our MDM, all enrolled laptops appear as monitored devices, and compliance status for encryption/lock/updates is visible and current in Vanta's evidence trail.

Report back: connection status, total devices monitored vs. total fleet size, any coverage gaps or failing compliance checks found, and next steps needed. If any step requires granting account-level authorization or accepting terms in Vanta or the MDM console, prepare everything needed but stop for human sign-off.
